decisions.rationale: Reproduced on a copy of the reviewed snapshot with the private solution applied: with the hook complete and fetchJson passing the signal but lacking the response.ok check, t4 fails ('expected null not to be null' at the HTTP 500 step) and t3 fails at 'Could not load this service (HTTP 404)'. Task 4's test therefore cannot pass from task 4 work alone, README 'How to test' discloses only the test 1 coupling, and the troubleshooting entry 'Task 4 tests pass but task 5 still fails' describes an unreachable state. Fix: move the ok check into task 4 rather than renumbering. One consistent relabel (shared with edu-err-1, edu-err-2 and edu-err-5): starter/src/api.js - the response.ok check comment becomes 'TASK 4 (part 2)' and the signal pass-through stays 'TASK 6 (part 1)'; starter/src/hooks/use-fetch.js - the TASK 4 comment says the hook relies on the task 4 ok check in api.js, and the ignore-the-AbortError line moves to its own 'TASK 6 (part 2)' marker; starter/src/pages/OverviewPage.jsx - 'TASK 5 (part 2)' becomes 'TASK 5', 'TASK 6 (part 3)' becomes 'Note (task 6)', 'TASK 8 (part 2)' becomes 'Note (task 8)'; starter/src/pages/ServiceDetailPage.jsx - TASK 3 says to finish task 4 first; README.md - task 4 includes the fetchJson ok check, task 5 is only the four overview screens, 'Files you edit' lists api.js for tasks 4 and 6, use-fetch.js for tasks 4 and 6, OverviewPage.jsx for tasks 5 and 7, and 'How to test' says to do task 4 before task 3 and lists every coupling (tests 1, 3 and 5 need task 4; test 1 also needs task 3). Test names, test files, failingTests and expected/on-completion.txt stay unchanged. Also rewrite the README troubleshooting entry to the real order (for example 'Task 4 fails at HTTP 500 - check the response.ok check in fetchJson').

Verified: README task 3 and the ServiceDetailPage TASK 3 comment require 'your hook from task 4', so working top to bottom reaches task 3 with the stub hook; the README never tells learners to work out of order. The critic's renumbering is not adopted because swapping tasks 3 and 4 changes test names and files bound in lab.json test.failingTests and expected/on-completion.txt. Fix: README.md 'How to test' instructs 'do task 4 before task 3' and lists every cross-task coupling, and the TASK 3 comment says the same, as part of: One consistent relabel (shared with edu-err-1, edu-err-2 and edu-err-5): starter/src/api.js - the response.ok check comment becomes 'TASK 4 (part 2)' and the signal pass-through stays 'TASK 6 (part 1)'; starter/src/hooks/use-fetch.js - the TASK 4 comment says the hook relies on the task 4 ok check in api.js, and the ignore-the-AbortError line moves to its own 'TASK 6 (part 2)' marker; starter/src/pages/OverviewPage.jsx - 'TASK 5 (part 2)' becomes 'TASK 5', 'TASK 6 (part 3)' becomes 'Note (task 6)', 'TASK 8 (part 2)' becomes 'Note (task 8)'; starter/src/pages/ServiceDetailPage.jsx - TASK 3 says to finish task 4 first; README.md - task 4 includes the fetchJson ok check, task 5 is only the four overview screens, 'Files you edit' lists api.js for tasks 4 and 6, use-fetch.js for tasks 4 and 6, OverviewPage.jsx for tasks 5 and 7, and 'How to test' says to do task 4 before task 3 and lists every coupling (tests 1, 3 and 5 need task 4; test 1 also needs task 3). Test names, test files, failingTests and expected/on-completion.txt stay unchanged.

Verified each sub-claim against the snapshot: (a) no test covers a malformed body, and ignoring the AbortError is never asserted (an AbortError-not-ignored hook mutant gives 8/8, see sme-err-1); (b) the TASK 8 comment answers the 'predict' question and nothing practises 'memo is a performance optimisation, not a correctness fix', while README task 8 is framed as a fix; (c) nothing practises 'state what an empty array means'. Fixes: (a) aborted handling becomes scored by the sme-err-1 Strict Mode check; for malformed, tests/t4-use-fetch-hook.test.jsx (same test name) adds a url whose stub returns a 200 Response with an unparseable body and asserts error is non-null, its message is not 'HTTP ...', data is null and loading is false (probe verified the solution passes this). (b) README task 8 and the StatusLegend.jsx TASK 8 comment reframe memo as a performance optimisation: it only skips work and never changes what is shown (for example retitle 'Skip the needless re-render'); the t8 test name is unchanged. (b) and (c): extend the lab.json cleanup.notes partial-objective sentence to name what-makes-a-component-re-render#o3's 'predict' and 'describe memo' clauses and loading-data-with-useeffect#o2's 'empty array' clause as practised on their topic pages. No objective id is removed.

The workload claim is not shown false by any evidence: this lab asks for two blank-stub builds (useFetch, the detail page) plus five more tasks across 8 files. The 25/30 figures are owned by course-owner directive 95387e98 (planning allowances, not hard timers), and that directive's own timing reconciliation accepted findings while keeping the numbers, so lab.json minutes stay unchanged. The critic's first remedy is in-lane because it removes typing, not objectives. Fix: starter/src/pages/ServiceDetailPage.jsx - ship a given presentational helper in the same file (level-2 name heading, StatusBadge, team, uptime, summary) that the page renders on success; the learner still writes useParams, the useFetch call, the loading and error branches and the useNavigate back handler. Conditions: no t1/t3 assertion changes and no objective id leaves lab.json; the shipped helper must not run before data loads, so the starter still fails t1 and t3 with stable messages; the TASK 3 comment and README task 3 wording match the edu-err-1/edu-err-2/edu-err-5 relabel. This trim does not validate the 25-minute figure; there is no pilot data.

Verified against the starter markers: README lists OverviewPage.jsx for task 6, but its 'TASK 6 (part 3)' and 'TASK 8 (part 2)' markers ask for no edit, there is no 'TASK 8 (part 1)' marker, and task 6 part 2 sits inside the TASK 4 comment in use-fetch.js, while README says every change happens at a TASK n comment. Fix: One consistent relabel (shared with edu-err-1, edu-err-2 and edu-err-5): starter/src/api.js - the response.ok check comment becomes 'TASK 4 (part 2)' and the signal pass-through stays 'TASK 6 (part 1)'; starter/src/hooks/use-fetch.js - the TASK 4 comment says the hook relies on the task 4 ok check in api.js, and the ignore-the-AbortError line moves to its own 'TASK 6 (part 2)' marker; starter/src/pages/OverviewPage.jsx - 'TASK 5 (part 2)' becomes 'TASK 5', 'TASK 6 (part 3)' becomes 'Note (task 6)', 'TASK 8 (part 2)' becomes 'Note (task 8)'; starter/src/pages/ServiceDetailPage.jsx - TASK 3 says to finish task 4 first; README.md - task 4 includes the fetchJson ok check, task 5 is only the four overview screens, 'Files you edit' lists api.js for tasks 4 and 6, use-fetch.js for tasks 4 and 6, OverviewPage.jsx for tasks 5 and 7, and 'How to test' says to do task 4 before task 3 and lists every coupling (tests 1, 3 and 5 need task 4; test 1 also needs task 3). Test names, test files, failingTests and expected/on-completion.txt stay unchanged.

Verified from the shipped mock (starter/mock-api.js matches ids only with /^\/api\/services\/([a-z0-9-]+)$/) and the identical test stub regex: a literal ':serviceId' fails the id pattern and gets an immediate 404 'unknown endpoint', so the page shows the HTTP 404 banner (or an empty service with an unfixed fetchJson), never 'Loading service...' forever; a solved-page mutant that fetches the literal path fails t3 at the Email Relay heading. Fix: README.md troubleshooting - replace the entry with 'Every detail page shows HTTP 404 - the URL must include the id from useParams, not a literal :serviceId', and add a separate entry 'Loading ... forever - check that your hook sets loading to false when the request settles'.

Verified in README.md: Setup ends in tests/ and the optional block runs 'cd starter' with no return to the lab folder, and does not mention that npm run dev holds the terminal. Fix: README.md optional dev block - prefix 'From the lab folder (cd .. if you are still in tests):' or use 'cd ../starter', and add one line about a second terminal and stopping the server with Ctrl+C. Same edit closes sme-err-5.

Reproduced: two hook mutants of the solved starter - one that aborts in cleanup but does not ignore the AbortError, one with a useRef already-fetched-this-url guard - each give 8/8 passed, because stubRoutedFetch, stubFailingFetch and stubEmptyListFetch ignore options.signal and no test renders in Strict Mode (starter/src/main.jsx does). Probe verified: a StrictMode render of MemoryRouter+App with an abort-aware stub reaches the Catalog API card with no error banner on the solution and fails both mutants. Fix: tests/helpers.js - make the shared stubs abort-aware like real fetch: return a promise that settles on a deferred tick (not an already-resolved promise), rejects with a DOMException named AbortError immediately if signal.aborted at call time, and also listens for the signal's abort event and rejects when it fires before settling (a call-time check alone misses the Strict Mode cleanup). tests/t6-abort-on-unmount.test.jsx (same test name) - add a StrictMode render of the overview with stubRoutedFetch that must reach the six loaded cards with no 'Could not load' text. Verified end to end on a scratch copy: with helpers.js switched to real Response objects and abort-aware stubs (deferred settle plus abort-event rejection) and the StrictMode block added inside t6, the solution passes all 8 tests plus the StrictMode check, the AbortError-not-ignored mutant fails it, and the shipped starter still fails all 8 named tests. Because the starter overview alone also passes the StrictMode block (it never shows an error banner), the block must stay inside the existing t6 test after the signal assertions so the starter keeps failing t6 with its current stable message. This scores loading-and-error-states#o2's aborted clause and the write-a-cleanup part of loading-data-with-useeffect#o3; the Strict Mode explanation clause stays in the existing partial-objective note.

Reproduced: a solved hook changed only to start with loading false passes t4, because result.current is read after renderHook's act() has flushed the Effect. Probe verified: capturing every render's return value and asserting the first render has loading true and data null fails that mutant and passes the solution. Fix: tests/t4-use-fetch-hook.test.jsx (same test name) - render via renderHook(() => { const r = useFetch(url); seen.push(r); return r; }) and assert seen[0].loading === true and seen[0].data === null in place of the current post-act read.

Reproduced: a solved fetchJson that parses with response.text() and JSON.parse fails 7 of 8 tests with misleading messages (for example t4 'expected null to deeply equal { from: 'a' }'), because jsonResponse returns a plain object with only ok, status and json(). Verified in the Vitest jsdom environment that the platform Response global exists and new Response(body, { status: 404 }) reports ok false. Fix: tests/helpers.js - jsonResponse returns new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' } }); stubPendingFetch's resolve and the inline t4 fetch mock use it too. Verified end to end on a scratch copy: with the Response-based helpers the solution and the text()+JSON.parse variant both pass all 8 tests, and the shipped starter still fails all 8. Apply together with the sme-err-1 abort-aware stubs; the solved run must be repeated after the helper change.

Reproduced: a solved overview that keeps the visible list in extra state synced by useEffect still passes t7, because act() flushes the sync Effect before assertions. Probe verified a scoring fix: with a recordRender('ServiceList') call in the shipped support file starter/src/components/ServiceList.jsx, one Degraded click renders ServiceList exactly once more for the derived solution and twice for the Effect-synced mutant. Fix: starter/src/components/ServiceList.jsx (support file, not a learner edit) adds recordRender('ServiceList'); tests/t7-lifted-filter.test.jsx (same test name) asserts renderCounts.ServiceList rises by exactly 1 after one filter click. This scores lifting-state-up#o3. what-makes-a-component-re-render#o3's 'describe memo' clause and the aborted clause are handled under edu-err-3 and sme-err-1.
Duplicate of edu-err-7, verified in README.md. Fix: the README optional-block change described under edu-err-7.
